assistant|sleep_tip_schedule: Go to bed and wake up at the same time every day, including weekends; aim for 7-9 hours of sleep
assistant|sleep_tip_environment: Make bedroom dark, quiet, and cool (around 60-67°F); invest in comfortable mattress and pillows; consider earplugs, white noise machine, or blackout curtains
assistant|sleep_tip_screen_wind_down: Avoid screens (phones, tablets, TVs) for at least an hour before bedtime
assistant|sleep_tip_stimulating_activiti: Avoid exercise, video games, or exciting movies at least 2-3 hours before bedtime; finish eating at least 2-3 hours before bedtime
assistant|sleep_tip_caffeine: Avoid consuming caffeine for at least 4-6 hours before bedtime; avoid nicotine products
assistant|sleep_tip_naps: If napping, keep it short (20-30 minutes) and avoid napping close to bedtime; eliminate naps if having trouble sleeping
assistant|sleep_tip_sunlight: Get morning sunlight exposure to help regulate circadian rhythms
assistant|sleep_tip_alcohol: Limit alcohol consumption as it can disrupt sleep patterns and reduce sleep quality
assistant|sleep_tip_diary: Consider keeping a sleep diary to track sleep patterns and identify patterns to adjust the routine
assistant|wind_down_tip_screen_replaceme: Replace TV before bed with reading a book, calming music, or gentle stretches; gradually reduce screen time by 30 minutes every few days
assistant|wind_down_tip_blue_light: Use blue light filtering glasses or apps like f.lux or Twilight if screens must be used before bed
assistant|wind_down_tip_tv_content: If watching TV before bed, choose calming content like nature documentaries, cooking shows, or gentle comedies
assistant|massage_roller_tip_pressure: Start with light pressure and gradually increase; use long, slow strokes
assistant|massage_roller_tip_areas: Focus on trouble areas like neck, shoulders, lower back; don't neglect legs (calves, thighs, glutes)
assistant|massage_roller_tip_breathing: Breathe deeply (inhale through nose, exhale through mouth) while rolling to help the body relax
assistant|snack_recommendation_trail_mix: Trail mix of nuts, seeds, and dried fruits is a satisfying snack rich in healthy fats, protein, and fiber
assistant|snack_recommendation_fresh_fru: Fresh fruit is a convenient, nutritious snack packed with vitamins, minerals, and antioxidants
assistant|snack_recommendation_energy_ba: Energy balls made with rolled oats, nuts, seeds, and dried fruits are a source of sustained energy
assistant|snack_recommendation_eggs: Hard-boiled eggs boiled on the weekend can be kept in the fridge for a quick protein-packed snack through the week
assistant|snack_recommendation_yogurt: Individual cups of Greek yogurt are a great source of protein and calcium; choose brands low in sugar and high in protein
assistant|snack_recommendation_veggie_hu: Carrot, celery, and cucumber sticks with hummus make a crunchy and healthy snack
assistant|snack_recommendation_smoothie: Protein smoothie blended from fruits, veggies, and protein powder is quick and can be taken on-the-go
assistant|snack_recommendation_apple_but: Apple slices with almond butter is rich in healthy fats, protein, and fiber
assistant|snack_recommendation_edamame: Edamame (boiled soybeans) is a protein-rich snack that can be steamed in the microwave in minutes
assistant|snack_recommendation_dark_choc: Dark chocolate with at least 70% cocoa content is a healthy treat rich in antioxidants, to be enjoyed in moderation
